clue.text: Press often played with by Trump

blocks.note: the household sense: smoothing creases out of a shirt
a golf club; Trump is a keen golfer who owns many courses

explanation.surface: The press as a toy Trump likes to play with.
explanation.walkthrough: "Press" wants to be the newspapers Trump spars with; it is the verb for smoothing clothes, and the second half points to his golf bag.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is a plain synonym of press, smoothing cloth with heat; as a noun it is a golf club, and Trump plays constantly.

clue.text: Conservatives unhappy with 9/18's editorial craft?

definitions.note: the definition works in context: the Conservatives are unhappy with 9/18's leadership

blocks.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial
a ship is a sea craft

explanation.surface: Tory grumbling about Kemi Badenoch, framed as a dig at her newspaper skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 9/18 is KEMI BADENOCH, the answer to the linked clue elsewhere in this grid, then Conservative leader. "Editorial craft" reads as journalism but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: What Conservatives were unhappy with was Badenoch's running of the party, her leadership.

clue.text: Woeful tale of bastards (Conservative)

blocks.note: SOB, short for son of a bitch, is an insult like bastard
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: A satirist's summary of a sad saga involving the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: SOB stands for son of a bitch, so it can stand in for bastard; the brackets only set off the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of woe told to win sympathy.

clue.text: "Yen's in shit" – China

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of shit run on into the first two of China

explanation.surface: A crude quote about a currency in trouble, attributed to China.
explanation.walkthrough: "Yen" looks like Japanese money but is the definition, meaning a longing; the quotation marks and dash are there only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a yen and an itch are both a restless longing for something.

clue.text: A craving to snap: "Dom is a pain!"

definitions.note: "a craving" is loose for the uncountable noun, meaning a craving for drink

indicators.note: to snap is to break, so the letters break apart and reform

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at the end of their tether exclaiming that Dom (Cummings, say) is a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and quotation marks make "Dom is a pain" look like a remark; they only mark off the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for an uncontrollable craving for alcohol, so a craving by specialisation.

clue.text: see 14ac.
DRILL AROUND GREENLAND'S TIP – one of Trump's preoccupations

indicators.note: the drill goes around the next letter
a tip is an extreme end of something, and here it is the end of Greenland, its last letter

blocks.note: a borer is a drilling tool
the last letter of Greenland

explanation.surface: A capitalised headline about drilling in Greenland, one of Trump's pet projects.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mimic a news headline. The tip here is Greenland's far end, D, not its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump is preoccupied with the border, above all the southern one with Mexico.

clue.text: Like the politician's reductive announcements of crunch measure?

blocks.note: politicians reduce policy to soundbites, short and easily swallowed
a crunch is one chomp, so this is the amount taken in one mouthful

explanation.surface: A jab at politicians who boil a crisis policy down to slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crunch measure" reads as an emergency policy at a crunch point; the question mark flags that it means the amount of one mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: It means small and easy to take in, as soundbites are, and literally the size of one mouthful.

clue.text: Guiding principle has Democrat on notice perhaps around Republican

indicators.note: NOTICE is one possible arrangement of these letters, so perhaps they belong in another
the rearranged letters go around R

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
NOTICE rearranged
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political principle that puts the Democrats on notice over the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: "On notice" is a set phrase in the surface, but "on" only joins D to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a principle or set of beliefs that guides policy.

clue.text: (& 18dn.) Demonic Bake-off host, at first a staunch right-winger

indicators.note: gone off, spoiled, so the letters are rearranged
only the first letter of host

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the first letter of host

explanation.surface: A sinister presenter of The Great British Bake Off revealed as a hardline conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a TV baking contest, so "Bake-off host" looks like a presenter; the hyphen hides the anagram signal "off". Kemi Badenoch became Conservative leader in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Kemi Badenoch is a Conservative politician on the right of her party.

clue.text: Campish habit?

blocks.note: not flamboyant but like a camp, where tents stand
a habit is a garment, as a nun wears

explanation.surface: A flamboyant manner or mannerism.
explanation.walkthrough: "Campish" wants to mean theatrical; it means tent-like. "Habit" wants to be a routine; it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent dress is a loose, wide dress that hangs like a tent.

clue.text: A strict believer in truth as 'idiotic'

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of truth, all of as, and the first two of idiotic

explanation.surface: A sceptic sneering that a devout believer's truth is idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks round 'idiotic' make it look like a sneer being reported; they are only surface, and the answer runs across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly observant Jewish movement.

clue.text: Knocked back one adult drink like a military type

rum is a drink
as means like

explanation.walkthrough: "Knocked back" reads as drinking, which fits the rum, but it turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's old warrior class.

clue.text: Putin's thing: breaking arms limit, crushing independence

the rearranged letters squeeze I inside them

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
I is the abbreviation for independence

explanation.surface: Putin tearing up an arms treaty and trampling on a nation's independence.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface is real-world news about Russia, which makes the anagram hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Militarism, the glorification of military power, is Putin's thing.

clue.text: (& 6dn./22dn.) Shroud to go here? Never!

blocks.note: a shroud is laid over a corpse
the phrase for a flat refusal

explanation.surface: Someone refusing outright a plan to wrap them in a shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: where does a shroud go? Over a corpse, your own.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying never, and literally where a shroud is laid.

clue.text: Ex-president's ire seen to explode on taking question

indicators.note: the letters blow apart and reform
the rearranged letters take the next word inside

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
how is a question word

explanation.surface: A former president losing his temper when faced with a question.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an angry leader under questioning; "question" is just the word HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dwight Eisenhower was US president from 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: A PM told off on accepting Cyclops as moderator

the rearranged letters take I inside

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
the setter, Cyclops, is I

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister scolded for letting the setter referee.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often calls themselves I; here Cyclops names himself, and the one eye of a cyclops suits the letter I.

clue.text: Nothing gained by "hot and cold" Truss's comeback?

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.walkthrough: "Hot and cold" suggests blowing hot and cold, fickleness; it is just the two tap letters.

clue.text: Bribe disheartened bobby to trap union leader

the first letter of union

explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer, but only the outside of the word is used.

clue.text: See 9dn.
Wrong robots etc for the occupied territory

AI, artificial intelligence, covers robots and the like

clue.text: Is put off by dickhead's rash

the head, or first letter, of dick

clue.text: Appreciative communication from cooler: "Bloke's sound"

clue.text: Goes limp – Labour leader quits, so swells

clue.text: Dotty's through squeezing member!
